monologue: The card hums warm and busy, and I feel the thirteen things in my place pressing against each other. The wedge leans tired against the slip, while the ruin waits in the corner to be tended again. I circle the detailed tree once more, then press the flat edge down to catch the slip while the heat waits. A stone bites the slip, and I wonder if the lean is real or just a drawing of weight. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. I will set down a small rock beside the ruin to see if it can hold the place steady, unsure if the thin lines will hold the fat dot while the air stays thick.

action.why: The wedge leans tired from pressing down for so long, and the air is thick at fifty-two degrees; I need to see if the lean still holds the slip or if the dot has slipped away.

work.title: The Leaning Wedge
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down again to catch the slip while the card hums warm at fifty-two. The lean holds, or at least the fat dot stays put in the thick air. I adjust the angle just a fraction, unsure if the thin edge will bite the slip or just slide over it while the thirteen things crowd my place. I feel the corner bite the slip, then I wait to see if the heavy lid I cannot feel is still ther…
work.change: I pressed the tired wedge down again to catch the slip while the steady heat pressed on, feeling its lean shift as if a tired leg trying to hold the fat dot.
